text: Achieve CNA onboarding agreements
Full draft forms for review before signature

This package contains a complete proposed Program Holder MOU, a separate confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement, and a separate limited non-compete and non-solicitation agreement. Each form has signature blocks for Elevate and Achieve. No signature, acceptance, or legal review has been recorded by preparing this package.
Confirmed instruction

The non-compete and non-solicitation restrictions apply during the relationship and for 12 months after it ends. This package does not adopt the three-year restriction found in the older public Program Host agreement.
Current account status

Achieve is approved for CNA onboarding and has an active Program Holder account. Its MOU remains unsigned. Account approval does not establish regulatory approval, clinical readiness, completed document review, verified banking, payment activation, or permission to begin an Elevate-funded class.
Complete before execution

Elevate will contract as 2Exclusive LLC-S, as instructed by Elizabeth Greene. Confirm Achieve’s exact contracting legal entity, both authorized signers, notice addresses, and the exact CNA training and clinical plan. Payment terms remain pending. The application states that Achieve has state approval; supporting evidence still requires review. The reported November 11, 2026 class date is a planning target, not a confirmed authorization or commitment.
Commercial schedule requires agreement

Elizabeth Greene confirmed that payment terms remain pending. No compensation rate, revenue split, tuition, minimum enrollment, referral volume, or payment deadline is established by this draft. Complete and sign Schedule A before committing to paid services. This draft does not import CDL pricing, Gary coordinator compensation, or a host-facility revenue split.
Review and deployment

Review the full language before replacing dashboard forms. These drafts have not been sent to Achieve for signature or published as binding portal terms. Indiana counsel should review the restrictions and the final contracting structure before execution. A 12-month duration alone does not establish enforceability.
Preparation sources

Prepared from Achieve’s submitted CNA application, the saved Program Holder account and checklist, existing Elevate portal responsibilities, and Elizabeth Greene’s 12-month instruction. Statutory reporting protections were checked against 18 USC 1833(b). Indiana courts’ commercial-court treatise describes the need for restrictions tied to a protectable interest and reasonable scope.

Review references: https://www.in.gov/courts/iocs/files/commercial-court-treatise.pdf and https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/1833. These references support review considerations and are not a certification of this draft’s enforceability.

1 Effective date and scope

The parties propose this MOU for CNA services identified in an executed Schedule A. It takes effect on the date of the last authorized signature. The proposed initial term is one year, unless Schedule A specifies otherwise. Renewal requires written agreement. Access to a dashboard alone does not execute this MOU.
2 Independent organizations

Each party remains an independent organization responsible for its own personnel, taxes, licenses, approvals, and business operations. Neither party may bind the other, promise funding, or represent that this arrangement creates employment, a joint venture, a franchise, or shared ownership. Only expressly authorized services and brand uses are permitted.
3 Elevate responsibilities

Elevate will identify its authorized referrals and program requirements; maintain the agreed administrative dashboard and enrollment records; communicate applicable funding and payment conditions; review submitted onboarding evidence; and identify the administrator responsible for coordination. Elevate may approve, defer, or decline an individual enrollment under the applicable program rules. No minimum referral or funding volume is promised.
4 Achieve responsibilities

Achieve will provide accurate organization and instructor credentials, maintain the approvals required for its services, designate a responsible Program Director, provide the agreed instruction and supervision, maintain safe facilities, and obtain valid clinical arrangements before clinical instruction begins. Achieve will not use this MOU as a substitute for state approval or offer services beyond its verified authority.
5 CNA training plan

Before a cohort is authorized, the parties will approve the syllabus, instructional hours, skills competencies, instructor assignments, class capacity, classroom or hybrid delivery arrangements, clinical location and availability, assessment procedures, attendance method, and completion reporting. Actual requirements must meet the applicable CNA program and clinical-site rules. No unverified number of hours or clinical placement is established by this MOU.
6 Enrollment and student contact

Achieve will record contact attempts and outcomes for Elevate referrals in the agreed dashboard; provide accurate class information; identify enrollment barriers; and promptly notify Elevate of no-shows, withdrawals, complaints, or unsafe conditions. Only authorized learners may be treated as Elevate enrollments. Learners retain their lawful choice of provider and rights to withdraw or complain.
7 Records and reporting

Achieve will keep accurate attendance, instruction, clinical and skills records, assessment results, completion evidence, and credential information within its authority. The parties will agree reporting deadlines in Schedule A. Corrections must preserve an audit trail. Neither party will mark attendance, competency, funding, or completion without supporting evidence.
Program Holder MOU continued
Schedule A and signatures  |  Form 1 of 3
8 Dashboard access and confidentiality

Each user must use an individually assigned account. Access is limited to authorized program work and records needed for that work. Credentials may not be shared. The separate NDA and limited non-compete agreement identify their own obligations and require separate execution. Signing one form does not record another form as signed.
9 Invoices and payment

Achieve will submit invoices and supporting service evidence through Elevate’s authorized dashboard or documented administrative process. Payment terms must be specified in signed Schedule A. Providing a setup link, creating a contractor record, or entering a recipient email does not verify banking or activate payment. Banking credentials must be entered only through the secure provider workflow, never ordinary email.
10 Safety compliance and review

Each party will comply with applicable laws, nondiscrimination requirements, program approvals, record protections, and lawful audit requests. Achieve will notify Elevate promptly of safety incidents, suspected record misuse, lapsed credentials, or clinical-site changes affecting delivery. Review must protect student privacy and stay within authorized access. An issue affecting safety or lawful delivery may require a pause while the parties coordinate a student-protection plan.
11 Ending the relationship

Either party may end this MOU on 30 days’ written notice. A material breach, loss of required approval, or immediate safety or security concern may justify suspending affected activity sooner. The parties will document learner communication, transfer or teach-out arrangements, record custody, and invoice reconciliation. Ending access does not waive verified amounts owed or eliminate confidentiality duties. The separate restriction agreement uses a 12-month post-termination period.
12 Written terms and disputes

Indiana law governs subject to mandatory applicable law. The parties will first seek a good-faith resolution and may agree to mediation; court relief remains available as permitted by law. Changes require a writing signed by both parties. This MOU and its completed Schedule A control the scope and commercial terms of this CNA relationship; unrelated public webpage pricing or restriction periods are not incorporated. If one provision is invalid, the remaining lawful provisions continue to the extent they can operate independently.

Confidentiality and non disclosure agreement
Achieve Training Institute CNA program  |  Form 2 of 3

Elevate contracting entity: 2Exclusive LLC-S. Program name: Elevate for Humanity Career & Technical Institute. The program name is used for identification and does not substitute for the contracting entity.
Program Holder: Achieve Training Institute. Exact contracting legal entity and any DBA: ________________________________________________.
Program: Certified Nursing Assistant CNA. Achieve contact: Nicole Newton, Program Director, subject to confirmation of signing authority.
1 Purpose and consideration

The parties expect to exchange nonpublic information to evaluate and carry out the authorized CNA relationship. In consideration of their mutual promises and authorized information access, each party agrees to protect information received from the other. This NDA takes effect on the date of the last signature and does not itself authorize enrollment, payment, or disclosure of student records.
2 Information covered

Confidential information means nonpublic information disclosed in connection with this relationship that is identified as confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential. It may include student and applicant records; nonpublic referral and business contacts; credentials; financial or funding records; pricing arrangements; curriculum and instructional materials; operating procedures; security information; and portal records. Information remains subject to any applicable third-party rights and privacy obligations.
3 Exclusions

Confidential information does not include information the recipient can demonstrate was lawfully known without a confidentiality duty before disclosure, became public without a breach, was lawfully obtained from a source free to disclose it, or was independently developed without using the protected information. A list of public facts may still be protected when its nonpublic selection or arrangement qualifies for protection.
4 Permitted use and access

The recipient may use protected information only for the authorized CNA relationship. It may disclose information only to personnel or professional advisers who need it for that purpose and are subject to appropriate confidentiality duties. No sale, unrelated marketing, unauthorized export, credential sharing, or use to divert referrals is permitted. The recipient remains responsible for people it authorizes to receive the information.
5 Security and student privacy

Each party will use reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, including access controls and secure transmission appropriate to the information. Student records may be accessed and shared only with the required authority, consent, or other lawful basis. This NDA does not replace a required data-sharing, clinical-site, or privacy agreement. Neither party may upload confidential records to an outside service without authorization and appropriate safeguards.
6 Incident response

A party discovering suspected unauthorized access, disclosure, or loss will promptly notify the other party through its designated security or administrative contact, preserve relevant evidence, cooperate in containment, and coordinate legally required notices. Notification must avoid unnecessary additional disclosure. Each party remains responsible for its own legal reporting obligations.
Confidentiality agreement continued
Duration protected reporting and signatures  |  Form 2 of 3
7 Required disclosure and protected reporting

A recipient facing compulsory legal disclosure may disclose only what is legally required and, when permitted, give advance notice so the disclosing party can seek protection. Nothing in this NDA prevents lawful communications with regulators, reporting suspected violations, responding to lawful process, seeking legal advice, or exercising rights that cannot lawfully be waived. No advance approval or notice is required for a legally protected report.
8 Trade secret immunity notice

Under 18 USC 1833(b), an individual may have immunity from federal or state trade-secret liability for a confidential disclosure to a government official or attorney made solely to report or investigate a suspected legal violation, or for a disclosure in a lawsuit filing made under seal. In a retaliation action for reporting a suspected violation, an individual may disclose the trade secret to the individual’s attorney and use it in the proceeding if documents containing it are filed under seal and further disclosure occurs only by court order. This notice includes individuals serving as contractors or consultants where the statute applies and does not authorize unlawful access.
9 Return retention and deletion

On request or when the relationship ends, the recipient will return or securely delete protected information within a reasonable documented period, subject to legally required retention, litigation holds, and inaccessible routine backups. Retained copies remain protected and may not be used for business purposes. Student-record disposition must follow applicable custody and retention rules rather than deleting records needed for learners or regulators.
10 Duration and ownership

The recipient’s use is limited throughout the relationship. Ordinary business confidentiality duties continue for 12 months after termination; trade secrets remain protected while legally qualifying as trade secrets, and student privacy, security, and retention duties continue for as long as applicable law requires. The separate non-compete and non-solicitation restrictions end after their stated 12-month period. Disclosure transfers no ownership or license beyond the limited authorized use.
11 Remedies and entire NDA

A party may seek remedies available under applicable law for an actual breach; no automatic penalty, injunction, damages amount, or fee entitlement is created by this draft. Indiana law governs subject to mandatory law. This NDA is the parties’ complete confidentiality agreement for this relationship unless a later signed writing expressly changes it. If a provision is invalid, independently enforceable provisions remain effective. Electronic signatures and counterparts may be used when lawful and authenticated.

Limited non compete and non solicitation agreement
Achieve Training Institute CNA program  |  Form 3 of 3

Elevate contracting entity: 2Exclusive LLC-S. Program name: Elevate for Humanity Career & Technical Institute. The program name is used for identification and does not substitute for the contracting entity.
Program Holder: Achieve Training Institute. Exact contracting legal entity and any DBA: ________________________________________________.
Program: Certified Nursing Assistant CNA. Achieve contact: Nicole Newton, Program Director, subject to confirmation of signing authority.
1 Purpose and consideration

The proposed restriction protects Elevate’s nonpublic information and relationships actually entrusted to Achieve through this CNA arrangement. In exchange for the mutual commitments and authorized access provided under the executed MOU, the parties agree to the limited obligations below. No restriction begins merely because this draft exists or a dashboard account was created.
2 Restricted period

The restrictions apply during the executed Program Holder relationship and for exactly 12 months after its termination or expiration. There is no automatic extension or tolling. The end date must be recorded in writing when the relationship ends. This form does not adopt a three-year post-termination restriction.
3 Protected relationships

A protected relationship means an Elevate-assigned learner or active referral, or an Elevate referral, clinical, employer, or funding contact, with whom Achieve had material dealings through this arrangement during the final 12 months of the relationship and whose nonpublic relationship information Achieve received through Elevate. A general public contact, an unsupported prospect, or a documented pre-existing Achieve relationship developed independently of Elevate is excluded.
4 Limited competitive activity

During the restricted period, Achieve will not use Elevate’s confidential curriculum, proprietary delivery materials, portal data, or nonpublic relationship information to reproduce an Elevate-derived CNA offering or divert a protected relationship into an outside competing CNA arrangement. The restriction concerns misuse of specifically entrusted information and contacts; it does not prohibit independently developed education, use of public CNA standards, general nursing employment, or Achieve’s otherwise lawful independent business.
5 Non solicitation and non circumvention

Achieve will not knowingly target a protected relationship using its Elevate access for the purpose of moving an authorized Elevate referral or enrollment outside the agreed workflow or avoiding an agreed invoice or payment arrangement. It will not instruct another person to do so on its behalf. Any claim of referral attribution must be supported by records. An unpaid or disputed invoice alone does not expand the scope or duration of this restriction.
6 Exceptions and learner choice

General advertising not targeted through Elevate’s nonpublic information, documented prior Achieve relationships, independently obtained contacts, protected reporting, and lawful learner choice remain permitted. An unsolicited inquiry is not automatically a breach; the parties should reconcile any actual referral attribution without restricting a learner’s rights. No agreement to fix market prices, divide unrelated customers, or prevent lawful work is intended.
Limited restrictions continued
Scope enforcement and signatures  |  Form 3 of 3
7 Defined scope

These restrictions apply only to the CNA relationship and protected contacts defined in this form. They do not impose a nationwide or statewide ban on competition and do not restrict unrelated programs, general public marketing, or service to the public using independently developed resources. No geographic exclusion area is created. A broader territory or activity restriction requires a separately reviewed and signed amendment.
8 Confidentiality remains separate

The NDA determines information-use, security, return, retention, and protected-reporting obligations. It does not extend this agreement’s non-compete or non-solicitation period beyond 12 months. Legally required student privacy protections and lawful trade-secret protections may continue independently.
9 Administration and evidence

Each party will keep records sufficient to identify authorized referrals, material relationship contacts, independent prior relationships, and the termination date. Records must be handled under the NDA. Neither party may fabricate attribution, retroactively label all customers as protected, or treat dashboard access as proof that every relationship qualifies.
10 Disputes and remedies

The parties will first attempt a good-faith resolution, while preserving the ability to request relief available under applicable law. Enforcement requires proof of an enforceable obligation and the facts supporting the requested remedy. No automatic injunction, fixed penalty, forfeiture of unrelated earnings, or entitlement to legal fees is created by this form. Indiana law governs subject to mandatory law. Courts retain authority to determine enforceability; this document does not guarantee it.
11 Written changes and severability

This agreement becomes effective upon the last authorized signature and is separate from the MOU and NDA. A change requires a writing signed by both parties. If a restriction is invalid, a court may disregard a genuinely separable provision to the extent permitted by law; this agreement does not ask a court to create a broader or new restriction. The remaining lawful and independent terms may continue.
12 Acknowledgment before signing

Each signer confirms authority to bind the identified organization, receipt of the complete form, an opportunity to obtain independent advice, and understanding of the 12-month limit and stated exceptions. No signer should execute this form while an essential party identity or material scope term is unresolved.
